subject: Next steps: Dedicated pool recommendation + GPU mix questions for Lattice Commerce
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-demo recap + Dedicated sizing clarifying questions

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the demo time today — really appreciated the clarity on the search+summarization workflow and the latency expectations for customer-facing queries. Quick recap and a few questions so our capacity worksheet and pricing estimate are aligned to your traffic profile.

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary workload: search → short answer generation for product pages (~70% of calls) and periodic deep multi-document summarization for long-form tickets (~30%).
- Current target SLOs: P95 generation latency <450ms for short answers; for long summaries acceptable up to 2.5s.
- Peak traffic: you mentioned spikes ~40 rps, steady-state ~12 rps.
- Compliance: must sit in a customer VPC for production, but you prefer Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) with the option to fall back to Hosted in emergencies.

Clarifying questions (will materially affect GPU mix & concurrency recommendations)
1) Token profile: can you confirm average input tokens and average output tokens for the two modes (short answer vs long summary)? If you have a percentile breakdown (50/95/99), paste that.
2) Session behavior: how long are typical sessions that benefit from a warm KV cache (i.e., multi-turn interactions that hit the same model state)?
3) Burst profile: are spikes simultaneous single-user storms (many independent short requests) or a few users generating many long requests?
4) Availability constraints: do you need SLA-backed reserved throughput during spikes (we can reserve burst capacity but that changes pricing)?

Initial recommendation (high level)
- Dedicated reserved pool in your VPC with a mixed-GPU strategy: a majority of L40S (cost-efficient, good for short low-latency inferencing) + a small number of H100s (or A100 if H100 not available in your region) to handle long-context summarization and heavy KV-cache sessions.
- Routing policy: route short answers to L40S cluster nodes with continuous batching and KV prefix caching enabled; long summarizations to H100s with larger memory and better long-seq perf.

Next steps
- If you can send the token-profile and a short CSV of request timestamps/examples (anonymized) I’ll run a quick sizing pass and return a model-by-model throughput projection and cost delta.
- I’ll loop Priyom (SE) for a technical deep-dive/bench session and share a capacity worksheet.

Attaching a stubbed worksheet in the next email.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — good write-up. Answers inline below.

Token profile (short versus long)
- Short answer (70%): median input ~35 tokens, median output ~120 tokens. 95th percentile output ~340 tokens.
- Long summary (30%): median input ~650 tokens, median output ~1,200 tokens; 95th percentile output ~2,400 tokens (we have some 4k+ cases but rare).

Session behavior
- KV-warm sessions: about 18% of requests are multi-turn sessions that reuse context (search session with follow-ups); typical session length 3–8 turns. Warm cache improves latency noticeably for these.

Burst profile
- Spikes are usually many simultaneous independent short requests (holiday promotions) rather than a single user generating long sequences. Peak concurrent short requests ~40 rps, sustained ~12 rps.

Availability / procurement notes
- Procurement will want a dedicated pool with an option to fail to Hosted in a DR event. They also requested a short doc on isolation and KMS integration.

Happy to share a small anonymized sample CSV (timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, is_multiturn) — sending after I scrub PII. Could you include guidance on whether we should target A100/H100 vs L40S for the long summaries? Cost sensitivity: we want to optimize for steady-state cost but not at the expense of P95 for short answers.

—Samir
CTO, Lattice Commerce
samir.patel@latticecommerce.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + Dedicated sizing clarifying questions

Great — thanks for the numbers, Samir. That token mix makes the mixed-GPU approach a good fit. A few concrete recommendations and ballpark sizing assumptions below so you have something actionable to discuss with Procurement.

Recommendation (detailed)
1) Dedicated reserved pool in your VPC (meets KMS/isolation ask). Configure automated fallback to Redwood Hosted API for DR.
2) GPU mix suggestion (initial pilot)
   - L40S x 6: serve short-answer traffic. L40S provides strong fp16/INT8 throughput for typical decoder-only workloads with good latency at lower cost than H100. Ideal for high QPS short responses.
   - H100 x 1: handle long summaries and heavy KV-cache sessions where model memory and long-seq perf matter. If H100 availability is restricted in your region, we can substitute A100-80GB x1 but expect slightly higher latency on the 2–4k token tails.

Sizing rationale (back-of-envelope)
- Short answer model (e.g., Llama2-13B-like fp16): one L40S can sustain ~300–600 short-answer requests/min depending on batching and average token length. With your steady ~12 rps (~720 rpm) and 40 rps peaks (~2400 rpm) we recommend 6 L40S to keep P95 headroom with continuous batching and a small per-request concurrency buffer.
- Long summary model: the H100 is sized for larger tokens and long contexts. Based on the 30% long-summary share and your spike profile, 1 H100 should support the background long jobs and some burst; if long-summary concurrency increases we’ll add a second H100.

Operational notes
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for session-heavy routes (the 18% multi-turn). That materially reduces tokens computed for follow-ups and improves effective throughput.
- Warmup: we’ll run a short benchmark to estimate effective warm-cache hit rates; if your sessions show >50% reuse, we may be able to reduce L40S count by 1–2.
- Pricing: reserved pool pricing and burst options are in the worksheet I’ll attach (capacity_worksheet_v1.xlsx).

Next steps (actionable)
1) Send the anonymized CSV you mentioned. Priyom will ingest and produce a TE (throughput estimate) + cost delta within 48 hours.
2) Schedule a 60-minute bench + architecture session (Priyom + infra) — propose Thu 4/17 10:00am PT or Fri 4/18 9:00am PT?
3) I’ll attach the capacity worksheet and a short doc covering VPC/KMS integration and isolation (for Procurement).

If that works I’ll follow up with the worksheet and a draft SOW/poC plan.

Thanks — Ben
